title: Is anyone actually live trading a bot on a prop firm?
author: MacaronWorking3293
selftext: Or are they just selling course like the classic 2016 FX guru strategy to a bunch of 18 y/o’s?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: a few people are, but prop rules quietly fight bots: news-window bans, consistency rules, and some firms restrict automated trading outright. read that page before you build anything for one. the course sellers tend to leave that part out.

replies.author: MacaronWorking3293
replies.body: Not live yet, just backtests and pretend money. I've tested \~50 strategies with full costs and no-peek checks, and almost everything failed. The one survivor (a simple US index dip-buy) has a real but thin edge: \~1.5% a year at prop-safe risk, so worse than a stocks & shares ISA. Scaling it across funded accounts could look big on paper, but I wouldn't trust that until it survives live. Most bot/prop stuff I've seen is course-selling.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
~1.5% a year after costs is more believable than most posts here. scaling it means every funded account holds the same trade, so one bad week hits all the daily loss limits at once.

I made Quantradin for the waiting part, the rule runs on live prices with fake money and costs nothing. quantradin.com if you want to park the dip-buy there.

replies.author: Extra844
replies.body: Quite live. Another thing when you go live you'll meet that time frames of calculation is vary, so again learn rules extremely carefully

comments.author: BenefitGrand8752
comments.body:
I’ve been testing a rule-based bot live with my own money through eToro’s API. That’s not a prop-firm account, so I can’t speak to that part specifically.

A lot of the work goes into handling disconnects, stale prices, delayed fills and preventing duplicate orders. Getting the bot to place trades is only one piece.

I’m still validating mine and wouldn’t claim a proven edge. For anyone selling a course, I’d want a verifiable live track record showing drawdowns and results after costs. Screenshots of winning trades wouldn’t convince me.

replies.body: Which assets are you trading? And what's the trading style os it like scalpers or trending following or something else?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Fair skepticism. The easy test is what they show as proof. A broker-verified live record over a few months, with drawdown and trade count, means a lot more than backtest screenshots or a payout picture. If the main product is the course, that tells you where the income comes from. It's also worth asking whether the bot survives on a funded account's drawdown limits, since many strategies look fine until one bad day ends the challenge.
